title: Builders in OMR: Approvals and Plot Checks Along the Corridor

seo.metaTitle: Builders in OMR, Chennai | House Construction | Hunter Property
seo.metaDescription: Building a house on OMR? Approvals change along the 45 km road. See which office approves your plot, what to check first and what our packages cost.

excerpt: OMR is one road but several approval routes. This guide explains how the stretch your plot sits on changes the paperwork, the checks and the build.
content:
One road, several rulebooks

OMR is one road on the map. For anyone building a house, it behaves like several.

Rajiv Gandhi Salai, which almost everyone still calls OMR, runs about 45 km from Madhya Kailash in Adyar down to Mahabalipuram. The northern part passes Perungudi, Thoraipakkam and Sholinganallur, inside Greater Chennai Corporation limits. Further south, through Navalur, Siruseri and Kelambakkam, you are outside the city, and the local body and CMDA take over.

That shift is the first thing our team checks on any OMR enquiry. The approving office decides the drawing format, the paperwork and how long you wait. Two plots twenty minutes apart on the same road can follow different routes. Many builders in OMR quote one way for the whole corridor. The approvals don't work that way, so neither do we.

Which stretch is your plot on?

A rough guide. Treat it as a starting point, not a ruling: the boundary that applies to your survey number is what counts.

StretchExamplesWho usually approves a houseWhat we look at first
Inside city limitsPerungudi, Thoraipakkam, Karapakkam, SholinganallurGreater Chennai Corporation (CMDA for larger buildings)Ground conditions, plinth level, how much floor area the plot allows
Outside city limitsNavalur, Siruseri, KelambakkamLocal body, with CMDA where it appliesLayout approval, ownership of the access road, water and sewerage

South of the city boundary

As the IT parks spread south, with the SIPCOT IT park at Siruseri the best known, farmland on either side of the road was turned into residential layouts. Plots here tend to be larger and quieter. They also come with a different set of questions.

  • Layout approval. Is the layout approved, by which body, and does the plot number in your sale deed match the approved layout plan? A plot in an unapproved layout can stall at the permit stage and again when you apply for a home loan.
  • The road in front. In newer layouts the internal roads should be handed over to the local body. If that hasn't happened, find out who maintains the road and whether your right to use it is written into your documents.
  • Water and sewerage. Many plots on this stretch rely on a borewell, and there is often no sewer line to connect to. Plan the septic tank from the start and keep it well away from the borewell and sump.

None of this is unusual for a growing suburb. It just needs answering before the drawings, not after.

Inside the city stretch

Closer to the city, plots are smaller and land is dearer, so most owners want every square foot of floor area the rules allow. The question shifts from "is this layout approved" to "what is under this plot".

The Pallikaranai marsh lies to the west of this stretch and the Buckingham Canal runs close to the road on the east. Parts of the ground between them are low, with groundwater near the surface, and the 2015 floods reached several OMR localities. So here the soil test and the plinth level take more of our attention than layout paperwork does.

Building next to a busy road

OMR carries heavy traffic, and the Phase 2 metro line under construction along much of it has added barricades and diversions. For a house site that matters in plain, practical ways.

  • Check whether a lorry can turn from the main road or service lane into your street, and at what hours.
  • Concrete pours and steel deliveries need a route that works on the day. Our site engineer confirms it before the first big pour.
  • If the plot fronts OMR, check the approved plan for any road-widening or street alignment line before fixing the front setback.

Plots on side streets a few hundred metres off the main road are usually easier to build on and quieter to live in. If you do build on the main road, think about noise at design stage: keep bedrooms to the rear, put the staircase and utility areas on the road side, and choose windows that close tightly. It costs little on paper and a lot to change later.

What it costs

Our packages are priced per sq ft of built-up area and stay the same along the whole corridor: Basic ₹2,199, Standard ₹2,399, Premium ₹2,699 and Ultra Luxury ₹3,199.

For example, a 2,000 sq ft house in the Premium package works out to about ₹54 lakh (2,000 × ₹2,699). Approvals, the soil test, compound wall, sump and interiors are priced separately. On the southern stretch, add a borewell and septic system to that list.

Why the right specification on OMR depends so much on what the land cost you is covered in our construction cost per sq ft on OMR guide, so we won't repeat it here.

How we handle an OMR build

  1. Site visit. We walk the plot, note how trucks will reach it, and ask neighbours about water levels and borewell depth.
  2. Document and authority check. We read the sale deed, patta and layout approval, and confirm which office will approve the plan: Greater Chennai Corporation inside city limits, the local body or CMDA further south. Our approved plot verification guide lists what we look for.
  3. Design. Drawings are prepared for the authority that actually applies, so you pay for them once.
  4. Approval. We prepare the application and follow it through with that office.
  5. Construction. Stage by stage, with a daily progress report from site.
  6. Payments. Linked to completed stages, not to calendar dates.

Start with where your plot is

Whichever builders in OMR you speak to, ask them one question before cost: which office will approve my plan, and how do you know? The answer tells you a lot.

Send us the survey number or layout name and the nearest landmark on OMR. We'll tell you which stretch it falls in, which office approves it and what we'd check before you commit. If you are still comparing localities, our builders in Chennai page covers the rest of the city.
faqTitle: Building a house on OMR: questions owners ask

faqs.question: Who approves a house plan on OMR?
faqs.answer: It depends on where the plot is. On the northern stretch inside city limits, including Perungudi, Thoraipakkam and Sholinganallur, the Greater Chennai Corporation approves individual houses, with CMDA for larger buildings. Further south, outside city limits, it is the local body or CMDA. Confirm it for your survey number before paying for drawings.

faqs.question: Is it better to buy a plot on the northern or southern part of OMR?
faqs.answer: Neither is better in general. The northern stretch has city services and shorter commutes but smaller, costlier plots and lower ground in places. The southern stretch offers larger plots but needs more checks on layout approval, road ownership, water and sewerage. Choose the stretch, then check the plot.

faqs.question: Do I need a borewell and septic tank on OMR?
faqs.answer: On many plots south of the city limits, yes, because there may be no sewer line and municipal water supply varies. Plan both at design stage and keep the septic tank well away from the borewell and sump. Inside the city stretch, check what connections your street actually has.

faqs.question: Does the metro construction on OMR affect building a house?
faqs.answer: Mainly through access. Barricades and diversions can limit when lorries and concrete mixers reach plots near the main road. We plan delivery routes and pour timings around them. Plots on side streets are usually less affected.

faqs.question: How much does a 2,000 sq ft house cost on OMR?
faqs.answer: With our packages, 2,000 sq ft costs about ₹44 lakh in Basic, ₹48 lakh in Standard, ₹54 lakh in Premium and ₹64 lakh in Ultra Luxury. Approvals, soil test, compound wall, sump and interiors are extra, and a borewell and septic tank may be needed further south.

faqs.question: How long does it take to build a house on OMR?
faqs.answer: It depends on the size of the house, the approval route and the ground. We give you a stage-wise schedule once the soil test and approval are in hand, and the daily progress report shows where the build stands against it.
